questions.prompt: With a uniform Beta(1, 1) prior, arm A converts 3 of 10 users. What is the posterior?
questions.explanation: Add conversions to α and non-conversions to β: Beta(1 + 3, 1 + 7) = Beta(4, 8).

questions.prompt: You test 10 metrics and want the family-wise error rate at 0.05 with Bonferroni. Which per-test threshold do you use?
questions.explanation: Bonferroni divides α by the number of tests: 0.05 / 10 = 0.005. Multiplying would make false positives far more likely.

questions.prompt: Raw BH ratios p·m/rank for two sorted p-values are [0.04, 0.021]. What are the adjusted p-values?
questions.explanation: BH takes a running minimum from the largest rank down, so the first value becomes min(0.04, 0.021) = 0.021. Adjusted p-values never decrease with rank.

questions.prompt: In A/A tests checked after each of 10 batches, the team stops at the first p < 0.05. Their false positive rate is closest to:
questions.explanation: Each look is another chance for noise to cross the threshold. With 10 looks the simulated rate is around 19%, nearly four times the nominal 5%.
